amelia: quick summary from this morning's nsys run on the INT8 rollout: weird host memcpy spikes during decoder dequant path, KV hit-rate looks fine (~92%) but tail latency doubles under burst. attaching timeline snippet below.

amelia: nsys capture: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt -o run_int8_deq ./serve_test --model rerun`
```
Timeline: kernel_launch | memcpy_h2d | dequant_int8_kernel | memcpy_d2h | kv_lookup | decoder_step
Observed: frequent memcpy_h2d right before dequant kernel, 5-8ms each, serializing subsequent kernels -> tail latency +80%
```

amelia: KV cache stats: hit_rate=0.923, avg_kv_size=1.2MB, eviction_rate low. Batching heuristic: dynamic batcher using latency_slo=50ms seems to inflate batch formation for short sequences.

raj: interesting — do we have per-stream SM utilization? memcpy spikes often mean host->device enqueue blocking on something (CPU-side memcpy or pinned buffer exhaustion). can you paste `nvprof --print-gpu-trace` segment or perfetto flame?

amelia: pasted small nvprof excerpt: `MemcpyHtoDPinned    6.2ms   43.1%` and `dequant_int8        0.9ms   12.4%`  (so dequant itself is cheap, overhead is host copy + kernel launch overhead)

mike: FYI i ran FP8 path on same workload earlier: FP8 dequant/scale is fused and uses less host traffic (we do device-side scale+cast). numbers: p50 latency down 18%, p95 down 35% vs current INT8 path. accuracy delta on our eval set: -0.6% perplexity (within roll threshold).

raj: that suggests our INT8 path still does dequant on cpu or does an extra memcpy for alignment. two avenues: 1) fuse dequant into the decode kernel (eliminate memcpy) or 2) switch to device-side dequant+cast using existing FP8 kernel patterns. fuse would be lower latency but more kernel complexity.

amelia: i tried simple device-side deq prototype (pushed branch feat/device-deq) — reduces memcpy_h2d frequency but we still see transient host stalls when batch sizes change rapidly. suspect the batching heuristic creates many tiny allocations pinned/unpinned.

perfbot: benchmark run complete (run id: br-20260318-14). workload: short-seq-chat, concurrency=24, model=redwood-7b-int8-variant. p50=42ms, p95=210ms, p99=450ms, kv_hit=0.921. Note: pinned buffer alloc count high (2.1k/s).

sylvia: could be allocator fragmentation. we saw similar before with cudaHostAlloc churn. maybe add a pinned buffer pool and reuse buffers for deq copies. also tune batcher: add micro-batching threshold (don't flush new batch until X ms or min tokens) so we avoid jitter.

mike: agree on pool. quick experiment: reusing a 2MB pinned ring buffer for copies cut memcpy_h2d count by ~70% in local test. code sketch: 
```
// pinned_ring.h pseudo
void* get_pinned_chunk(size_t len) { idx = atomic_fetch_add(&head, len) % BUFSIZE; return base + idx; }
```

raj: other thought: kernel selection policy chooses int8_deconv for seq_len<32 due to perf table; but that path triggers a different buffer layout requiring copy. if we relax selection to favor fused kernels for <32 we may reduce copies at slight compute cost. worth testing.

amelia: plan for next steps: 1) try pinned ring reuse + re-run nsys to confirm memcpy drop 2) test device-side dequant branch end-to-end and compare p95/p99 3) experiment with kernel selection tweak (prefer fused kernel for short sequences) and measure throughput impact. I'll create a canary rollout with feature flags.

mike: if you need quick perf harness i can spin up synthetic runner with concurrency sweep. canary config: 5% traffic, metrics: p95, p99, kv_hit, error_rate.

amelia: thanks — assigning tickets: RH-2153 pinned-buffer-pool, RH-2154 device-deq-fusion, RH-2155 kernel-selection-policy. will post nsys trace link once first re-run is done.

sylvia: also add an eval check for token-level accuracy for the device-deq path (small eps shifts can leak into generation loops). set auto-rollback on >1% regression.

raj: +1. if someone wants to pair on the nsys analysis i can help tonight. short-term mitigation: increase batcher flush threshold to 4ms to reduce micro-batches (flip flag).

amelia: flipping flush threshold on prod-sim and re-running now. will post results in this thread. thanks all :thumbsup:
